laws.rule: Baja California charges a state lodging tax (Impuesto sobre Servicios de Hospedaje) on lodging received in the state: hotels, motels, villas, cabins, campgrounds, caravan parks, tourist marinas, timeshare, and stays booked through digital platforms. The guest is the taxpayer and the host collects it. The rate is set each year in the state revenue law: 5.0% in the 2025 law, 7.0% for motels (Ley de Hacienda del Estado de Baja California, art. 127 to 130; Ley de Ingresos del Estado 2025, art. 6). The 2026 revenue law was not read.

Baja California's alcohol law bans selling alcohol on the street, in parks and in public squares, except under a temporary permit from the municipality (Ley para la Venta, Almacenaje y Consumo Público de Bebidas Alcohólicas, art. 23). Licensed venues may not open before 10:00 or go past 03:00 the next day, and councils can cut those hours (art. 17). Venues must stop selling on dates set by federal election rules and on days a council or the governor orders for safety, and must not serve anyone under 18 (art. 26).

Baja California's smoke-free law bans smoking or keeping a tobacco product lit in 100% smoke-free spaces (enclosed public places) and in public and private schools (Ley de Protección contra la Exposición al Humo de Tabaco, art. 15). Restaurants and bars must enforce the ban inside; a venue may offer a smoking area only if it meets the law's conditions (art. 17). Tobacco can't be sold to minors or as single cigarettes (art. 15).

items.text: The Ley para la Venta, Almacenaje y Consumo Público de Bebidas Alcohólicas del Estado de Baja California, last reformed in the Periódico Oficial of 30 January 2026, forbids licensees, managers or staff from selling or allowing the consumption of alcoholic drinks by anyone under 18 (art. 26). Venues authorised to sell alcohol for consumption must also refuse entry to anyone under 18, anyone clearly drunk or obviously under the influence of a drug, and people the law describes as having a mental deficiency (art. 25).

Article 23 bans the sale, storage for sale, or sale for consumption of alcoholic drinks in unlicensed places; on the public street and in parks and public squares, except under a temporary municipal permit; in workplaces, educational centres or places of religious congregation; at fairs, kermesses, shows or any other children's event; in government offices; and in hospitals, police, fire, prison, correctional and similar premises. Municipal rules may allow limited exceptions inside cinemas, theatres and similar performance venues (art. 23 IV).

Article 17: licensed sale in a closed or open container must not start before 10:00 or go past 03:00 the next day. The hours in the permit follow this law and the municipal regulation; councils may reduce hours, temporarily or permanently, and may authorise temporary event permits, but those event hours still cannot exceed the law's maximum. Councils also set wholesale delivery hours to licensed venues.

psychoactive-substances.notes: This is state law on licensed sale, storage and public consumption. It is not a general adult drinking-age statute for private possession at home. Councils issue permits and may tighten hours. The official compilation was read in the 30 January 2026 version.
